messages.subject: Getting error in bootstrapping
parts:
Dear All,

I have a meditation model. When I run my model using sem it runs. But when I use bootstrapping, I get the following error. I brought my syntax and model at the end of the email. I also should mention that I have a pretty small sample size ( do not know it is relevant or not)
I would appreciate it if could help me in this regard. Thanks!

Error in eigen(VarCov, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE) :
  infinite or missing values in 'x'
In addition: Warning message:
In lav_model_nvcov_bootstrap(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: 1 bootstrap runs failed or did not converge.
***************

medfit <- sem(mediation.model, data = x_med, meanstructure = TRUE)

medfit <- sem(mediation.model, data = x_med, meanstructure = TRUE,
              se = "bootstrap", bootstrap=500)


mediation.model2 <- ' 

d=~d1+d2+d3+d4+d5

e3=~e31+e32+e33+e34
e4=~e41+e42+e43+e44

t1=~t11+t12+t13+t14
t2=~t21R+t22+t23
t4=~t41+t42+t43+t44
t5=~t51+tl52+t53+t54

             # mediator

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Getting error in bootstrapping
parts: I have a pretty small sample size ( do not know it is relevant or not)

Can you be more specific?  "Small" could be < 200 for a model this large.  If < 100 and you have few unique values (e.g., 5-point Likert scale), it is plausibly common for bootstrap samples to have the same value for a variable, or for 2 variables to be collinear in a bootstrap sample, which would cause it to fail.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Getting error in bootstrapping
parts:
May I ask a related question?

With se = "bootstrap", I know that failed bootstrap runs will be reported and excluded, with a message like this one:
"lavaan WARNING: 1 bootstrap runs failed or did not converge."

However, will the bootstrap function also capture bootstrap runs with errors (not nonconvergence or failure in pass the post.check) , as in the example of the first post. include these runs with errors in the count of "bootstrap runs failed or did not converge", and exclude them from the computation of CIs and SEs?

If yes, then, *maybe*, the error message can be safely ignored, just like ignoring bootstrap runs that failed, provided that the number of these bootstrap runs is small.

-- Shu Fai
